From f40a6be4a4e4985aef5365007e2459d757f26bdd Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Heiko Stuebner <heiko.stuebner@theobroma-systems.com>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2020 23:56:06 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] serial: 8520_port: Fix function param documentation

The parameter is named p while the documentation talks about up.
Fix the doc to be in line with the code.

Fixes: 058bc104f7ca ("serial: 8250: Generalize rs485 software emulation")
Suggested-by: Andy Shevchenko <andy.shevchenko@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Heiko Stuebner <heiko.stuebner@theobroma-systems.com>
Reviewed-by: Andy Shevchenko <andriy.shevchenko@linux.intel.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20200517215610.2131618-2-heiko@sntech.de
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/tty/serial/8250/8250_port.c b/drivers/tty/serial/8250/8250_port.c
index 4d83c85a7389..bf2722e5e3aa 100644
--- a/drivers/tty/serial/8250/8250_port.c
+++ b/drivers/tty/serial/8250/8250_port.c
@@ -1432,7 +1432,7 @@ static void serial8250_stop_rx(struct uart_port *port)
 
 /**
  * serial8250_em485_stop_tx() - generic ->rs485_stop_tx() callback
- * @up: uart 8250 port
+ * @p: uart 8250 port
  *
  * Generic callback usable by 8250 uart drivers to stop rs485 transmission.
  */
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/tty/serial/8250/8250_port.c`**
   - The documentation for the function `serial8250_em485_stop_tx()` was modified. 
   - The parameter name in the documentation was changed from `@up` to `@p` to accurately reflect the actual parameter name used in the function definition.

### Relationships
- The modification in the documentation aligns the parameter name in the comments with the actual code, thereby improving clarity and consistency. This change addresses a discrepancy that could lead to confusion for developers reading the code, ensuring that the documentation accurately describes the function's parameters. The patch is part of a broader effort to maintain code quality and clarity, as indicated by the references to previous fixes and suggestions from other developers.

The documentation for the function `serial8250_em485_stop_tx()` incorrectly referred to the parameter as `up` instead of `p`, leading to potential confusion for developers regarding the function's implementation and usage. This inconsistency could result in misunderstandings when maintaining or using the code, as the documentation did not match the actual parameter name in the function signature.
